title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in this continuation of La Longue Marche, Grothendieck tries to 'schematize' discrete abelian groups (Z, Z^n, Z/n, and their profinite completions) over S_0 = Spec Z. The aim is a Z-integral version of what over a field of characteristic 0 would be the pro-algebraic hull, roughly profinite completion times pro-unipotent completion. This is part of his schematization programme for homotopy types over Spec Z.

Step 1 (end of the previous page and top of this one). The projective limit of the vector group schemes (G_a, multiplication by n) is the affine scheme E^1 = Spec(lim_n Z[T/n]) = Spec(Z + T Q[T]). The ring Z + T Q[T] is the ring of rational polynomials with integer constant term (a classical non-noetherian D+M ring). E^1 is a commutative group scheme over Spec Z with these fibres:
- over F_p the fibre is Spec F_p, the trivial group, since T Q[T] ⊗ F_p = 0;
- the generic fibre is G_{a,Q}.
For Z^n one gets (E^1)^n: trivial fibres at every prime and generic fibre G_{a,Q}^n. Functorially, E^1(A) = lim(A, ×m) = {(x_n) : x_n = m x_{mn}} ≅ Hom_Z(Q, A). This is A when A is a Q-algebra and 0 when nA = 0.

Step 2 (this page). Let G be a finitely generated abelian group, written multiplicatively. Let Ĝ be its profinite completion and Ĝ_{S_0} = lim_i (G/M_i)_{S_0} the corresponding profinite constant group scheme over Z (formula (50)). Here the M_i run over the finite-index subgroups of G that are free of finite type. For such a module M, the scheme M = V̌(M) = Spec Sym_Z(M^∨) is the vector group representing A ↦ M ⊗ A (formula (53)).

Grothendieck asserts a canonical exact sequence (51):
1 → E°(G) → lim E(G) → Ĝ_{S_0} → 1.
The neutral component is E°(G) = lim_i M_i ≅ lim_n nM (formula (52)), where the transition maps are induced by the inclusions M_j ⊂ M_i. The nM are cofinal among the M_i, and after identifying nM with M the inclusion becomes multiplication by n. The next page then gives E°(G) ≅ (E^1)^r after choosing a basis of some M_0.

So the schematization of G over Z is an extension of the constant profinite group Ĝ by a 'pro-vector group' whose fibres at all primes p are trivial and whose generic fibre is G_a^r. This is an integral model of the characteristic-0 hull 'Ĝ × unipotent completion'. In characteristic p the unipotent part degenerates completely, its role being absorbed by the profinite part.
errors: Exactness of (51) as a sequence of affine group schemes or fpqc sheaves after passing to the limit is asserted without argument. It is plausible, since the transition maps are affine and each level is a split extension of a constant group by a vector group, so lim^1 issues vanish. Still, it is not verified on the page.
The page is unclear about what the object 'E(G)' at finite level is. It is presumably defined on earlier pages: the G_n schemes interpolating between Z and Z/n.

ideas.what: lim_n (G_a, ×n) over Z is represented by Spec(Z + T Q[T]); it has trivial fibres at all primes and generic fibre G_{a,Q}, and represents A ↦ Hom_Z(Q, A).
ideas.modern_name: 'universal cover' / inverse limit along multiplication of a vector group; D+M ring Z+XQ[X]
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ring: classical commutative algebra (Gilmer; Brewer–Rutter, D+M constructions, 1970s). Universal-cover type limits: Fontaine, Scholze–Weinstein (for p-divisible groups).

ideas.what: Exact sequence 1 → (pro-vector group lim_n nM) → schematization of G → Ĝ_{S_0} → 1 over Spec Z for a finitely generated abelian group G.
ideas.modern_name: integral affine/pro-algebraic hull of a discrete abelian group; schematization of K(G,1) over Z
ideas.usually_credited_to: Toën (affine stacks 2006; 'Le problème de la schématisation de Grothendieck revisité', 2020); over fields: Hochschild–Mostow pro-algebraic hull
ideas.where_published: Schematization problem stated in Pursuing Stacks and in the letter to Breen (1975); this explicit construction does not appear there as far as I know.

ideas.what: Neutral component as a limit over finite-index lattices M_i, cofinal with nM, identified with (E^1)^r via a basis.
ideas.modern_name: inverse limit of vector groups V̌(M)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's integral schematization of Z combines a profinite constant part Ẑ_{S_0} with a pro-vector part Spec(Z+TQ[T]) whose fibres in characteristic p are trivial. Toën's later solution of the schematization problem over Z instead uses Spec of the ring of integer-valued polynomials Int(Z). Its fibre over F_p is (Z_p)_{F_p} and its generic fibre is G_a, so profinite and unipotent behaviour are fused into a single flat group scheme. Grothendieck's split description (extension of Ẑ by lim(G_a, ×n)) is a different, non-flat-in-the-same-sense candidate. A comparison between the two (is there a natural map from the binomial-ring object to Grothendieck's extension, and which corepresents the right homotopy theory?) does not seem to be in the literature.
missed.quote: on aura une suite exacte canonique (51) 1 → End°(G) → lim End(G) → (Ĝ)_{S_0} → 1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This bears on the choice of integral models in schematic or affine homotopy theory over Z (Toën, Horel, Kubrak–Shuklin–Zakharov on derived binomial rings) and documents Grothendieck's own concrete attempt.

missed.claim: This is an explicit construction of a schematization over Spec Z of finitely generated abelian groups and their profinite completions, apparently intended as the K(G,1) case of a schematization of homotopy types over Z. It is a thread of the schematization programme, and only partially taken up later.
missed.quote: C'est donc un schéma en groupes sur Spec Z dont toutes les fibres sont réduites au groupe unité, sauf la fibre générique, qui est G_{a,Q}^n.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical evidence of how Grothendieck envisioned integral schematization in the Longue Marche period (around 1981). It is of modest mathematical novelty.

deep.surprise_reason: The individual facts are elementary: Z+TQ[T] is a known ring, and inverse limits of vector groups are standard. What is notable is an explicit, unpublished Grothendieck construction of an integral schematization of discrete abelian groups, as an extension of Ĝ_{S_0} by a pro-vector group. It differs from the later Int(Z)-based approach of Toën, and is of interest mainly historically and for comparison.
transcription_corrections: The symbol transcribed 'End' / 'End°' in (51) and (52) looks in the image more like 'Env' / 'Env°' (envelope, enveloppe), i.e. the schematic hull of G rather than an endomorphism scheme. This is uncertain, but it fits the meaning: the next page's 'End^0(Z) ≅ E^1' reads naturally as Env^0(Z).
The crossed-out word in line 3 is 'générique', and 'fibre générique' is then rewritten after it; the text should read 'sauf la fibre générique, qui est G_a^n_Q'.
The 'G' throughout is a blackboard/script G (an abstract abelian group written multiplicatively), not a group scheme.
In (52) the second line reads '≃ lim_n n.M' with M underlined (the vector group of nM).
